explanation: Save the next node before pointing the current node back to the reversed prefix. After the scan, the previous node is the new head. All nodes are reused.
attribution: Original C# implementation and explanation authored for EPI Practice from the displayed problem contract.
correctness: previous is always the correctly reversed processed prefix, and head begins the untouched suffix. Saving the next node before changing head.Next keeps the suffix reachable. Linking the current node to previous extends the reversed prefix by one node. When head becomes null, previous is the complete reversed list.
walkthrough: For [3,8,-2], redirect 3 to null, then 8 to 3, then -2 to 8. The final previous pointer is the original -2 node, producing [-2,8,3].
edgeCases: One node points to null both before and after reversal.
No replacement data nodes are allocated.
The original tail becomes the new head.
